text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Planned limited maintenance at Port Harcourt refinery has been put off indefinitely by the inability of management to obtain letters of credit for the imporation of spare parts.
- Directorate of Military Pensions is looking for 480 million naira to pay retired armed forces personnel.

- A final report on reforming the capital market is likely to be submitted to government this month. Although details have not been released there are indications it may propose the resumption of the privatisation programme.
- 10,000 containers abandoned at Nigerian ports may be auctioned.

- Offshore drilling for oil has begun near Lagos by Folawiyo Petroleum Company, an indigenous venture. So far the company has encountered gas in one well, but managing director said it is premature to speak of a discovery.
- Federal government may soften its stance on oil joint- ventures by amending working agreements.
